strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 150+ tasks spanning multiple benchmarks (SimplerEnv, LIBERO) and real-world settings with 3 robots, demonstrating thorough validation
Strong empirical results on long-horizon real-world temporal tasks (+26 points vs CogACT), addressing a genuine limitation in existing VLA models that ignore temporal dependencies
Well-motivated problem with clear examples (e.g., Push Buttons) illustrating the non-Markovian nature of manipulation and why current Markovian VLA models fail
Excellent reproducibility with detailed hyperparameters, training procedures, task descriptions, and implementation details enabling future work
Thorough ablation studies quantifying contributions of memory type, length, retrieval, fusion, and consolidation mechanisms
Sound technical approach combining cross-attention retrieval, adaptive gating fusion, and similarity-based consolidation with reasonable design justifications
Robustness evaluation under 7 types of OOD conditions, demonstrating generalization on simulated and real-world tasks
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and cognitive science motivation that frames the problem compellingly
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: components are largely combinations of well-established techniques (cross-attention, element-wise gating, cosine similarity consolidation) without fundamental innovation

Insufficient analysis of memory mechanism: no visualization of learned perceptual vs. cognitive representations, no tracking of which historical entries are retrieved, no investigation of consolidation effectiveness

Weak justification for architectural choices: perceptual and cognitive streams differ by only 0.1% individually yet provide +8% combined; consolidation provides only +5%; alternative fusion mechanisms not compared

Modest gains on standard benchmarks undermining universal applicability: SimplerEnv-Fractal +4.6% vs CogACT (+0.9 vs π0-Beta), LIBERO +3.3% vs CogACT - suggests temporal memory helps only on specific task types
Severe generalization failure under camera view changes (42-58% success vs 76-92% baseline) barely discussed despite being a major limitation contradicting robustness claims

Confounded comparisons with baselines: different input modalities (third-person RGB only vs. wrist camera + proprioceptive state for π0-FAST) make direct comparison unreliable regarding the source of improvements
Limited temporal horizon and unclear scaling: memory length L=16 at 30fps ≈ 0.5 seconds; unclear why L=64 drops to 67.7% or how method scales to true long-horizon tasks

Missing critical analyses: no failure case investigation, no error categorization, no computational cost discussion, no side-by-side trajectory comparisons with baselines, insufficient explanation of when/why the method works

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 150+ tasks with 500+ variations spanning SimperEnv, LIBERO, Mikasa-Robo, and real-world validation—exemplary scope for robotics research
Strong empirical results with clear patterns: modest gains on non-temporal tasks (+3.3% on LIBERO) but substantial improvements on temporal tasks (+26% on real-world temporal tasks vs. CogACT)
Rigorous experimental methodology with thorough ablations (Tables 6-7, 10-14) demonstrating each component contributes meaningfully
Excellent reproducibility with extensive implementation details, hyperparameters, training procedures, and promised code/model release
Well-motivated problem formulation: clearly articulates non-Markovian nature of manipulation and limitations of naive temporal context approaches
Cognitive science-grounded dual-memory framework (working memory + episodic memory) provides strong conceptual organization
Practical design with minimal inference overhead (3.6% latency increase, +0.8GB memory) enabling real-world deployment
Insightful memory retrieval analysis (Figure 10) showing model retrieves decision-relevant historical frames rather than redundant patterns
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: combines existing components (cross-attention retrieval, gate fusion, cosine similarity consolidation) in straightforward manner rather than introducing fundamentally new techniques
Memory design choices lack thorough justification: no comparison of alternative architectures, fusion mechanisms, or consolidation strategies; marginal ablation improvements (Table 12: 84 vs 78)
Inconsistent memory length hyperparameter across benchmarks (16 for most, 256 for real-world temporal) with length ablation only on SimplerEnv-Bridge; unclear sensitivity across task types

Incomplete baseline comparisons: π0-FAST uses additional inputs (wrist camera, proprioceptive state) making direct comparison unequal; temporal baselines (Table 17) not consistently applied across all benchmarks
Modest gains on non-temporal tasks (+3.3% on LIBERO) suggest limited general applicability; unclear which task distributions benefit most from temporal modeling
Real-world evaluation details underspecified: only 12 tasks, no data efficiency analysis vs. baselines, no ablation on demonstration requirements (50-300 demos)
Missing operational details: episode initialization behavior before memory builds up, maximum episode length, memory accumulation across episodes, distribution shift handling
Cognitive science framing somewhat disconnected: 'gist representation' reduced to EOS token may not capture richness of semantic abstraction; biological memory connection feels loose
Limited failure analysis: no discussion of failure modes, cases where temporal memory doesn't help, or task characteristics determining when method is necessary

Attention mechanism details insufficiently justified: timestep PE added to K but not V (asymmetry unexplained), no attention weight visualization, consolidation operation (in-place vs. new entry) unclear

strengths: Well-motivated problem: clearly articulates temporal dependency limitations in current VLA models with effective examples (Push Buttons task)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 150+ simulation tasks, 500+ variations, 3 robots, 6 benchmarks, plus 12 real-world tasks on actual hardware
Strong empirical results on long-horizon real-world temporal tasks: +26 improvement over CogACT, demonstrating practical value where temporal reasoning matters most
Efficient implementation with minimal overhead: only 3.6% latency increase despite adding memory mechanisms; detailed inference efficiency analysis provided
Solid technical execution: memory module is cleanly designed with interpretable components (retrieval, gating, consolidation); cross-attention and gate fusion properly implemented
Thorough reproducibility: detailed hyperparameters, training procedures, ablation studies, and commitment to release code/models/logs/videos
Extensive ablation studies: memory type, length, retrieval mechanisms, fusion methods, and consolidation strategies systematically evaluated
Real-world robustness evaluation: OOD testing across backgrounds, distractors, lighting, occlusion, and container variations
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: combines only standard, well-established techniques (cross-attention for retrieval, gating mechanisms, cosine similarity consolidation). Individual components are not novel; core insight that 'memory helps temporal tasks' is unsurprising

Misleading baseline comparisons: main paper compares against non-temporal VLA models (π0, CogACT). When compared to actual temporal baselines (Table 17, Appendix J), gains are much smaller (e.g., +3.3 on LIBERO vs +14.6 vs non-temporal). Questions whether improvement comes from temporal modeling generally or this specific approach

Insufficient analysis of when/why memory helps: LIBERO (+3.3) vs SimplerEnv-Bridge (+14.6) gap unexplained; memory length ablation shows 4/16/64 yield similar performance (67.7-71.9%), suggesting design choices are arbitrary rather than crucial
Weak zero-shot generalization (47% average on Table 16): only marginal improvement on unseen task categories, limiting practical applicability despite claims of strong generalization

Unfair input modality comparisons: many baselines (π0, π0-FAST marked with *) use proprioceptive and wrist-camera inputs while MemoryVLA uses only third-person RGB, making quantitative comparison problematic

Superficial cognitive science framing: connection to human memory is loose (cross-attention ≠ working memory operation; token averaging ≠ consolidation). Takes up space without adding technical insight

Limited temporal context despite claims: memory length=16, action chunk=16 gives ~32-frame context, yet real-world tasks span 1600+ frames (Table 9). Paper doesn't explain how model handles such large gaps or whether it truly captures 'long-term' dependencies
Lack of statistical rigor: no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests; results are point estimates; some improvements are modest (±3.3) with unknown variance

Limited real-world scope: only 12 tasks, 2 robots, relatively simple manipulation (pick, place, stack). Severe OOD degradation under unseen camera views (92%→42% on Pick Coke Can). No complex multi-step assembly or truly long-horizon real-world validation

Unjustified design choices: memory consolidation only when full (reactive), single cognitive token despite redundancy being claimed as key, specific gating mechanisms not ablated against alternatives, no learned similarity metrics for consolidation

Incomplete analysis: missing ablations on retrieval mechanisms, action expert architecture, why separate cognition/perception attention layers; unclear whether model learns temporal reasoning or just memorizes visual details
Incremental over temporal baselines: Table 17 shows MemoryVLA performs best, but margins are often small, suggesting the contribution is engineering-focused rather than conceptually novel

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 150+ tasks on 3 robots in simulation and real-world, demonstrating strong and consistent improvements (+14.6 Bridge, +26 real-world temporal)
Clear and well-motivated problem addressing genuine limitation of existing VLAs for long-horizon, temporally-dependent manipulation tasks
Thorough ablation studies (Tables 6-7) demonstrating each component contributes, with extensive robustness analysis under OOD conditions (backgrounds, lighting, distractors, occlusion)
Strong reproducibility commitment with detailed hyperparameters, data augmentation, implementation details, and promise to release code/models/videos
Technical soundness with practical design choices (SE-bottleneck compression, efficient memory consolidation preventing bloat) and minimal inference overhead (3.6%)
Insightful memory retrieval visualizations (Fig. 10) showing model retrieves decision-relevant historical context, validating design approach
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty - individual components (cross-attention retrieval, gate fusion, similarity-based consolidation) are standard techniques; contribution is primarily in engineering and combination
Temporal-context VLA baselines (CronusVLA, TraceVLA, 4D-VLA, MAP-VLA) relegated to appendix with only modest gains over them, should be prominently featured in main tables

Key design choices lack justification: Why separate perceptual/cognitive memories specifically? Why cosine similarity for consolidation? Task-dependent memory length (16 vs 256) offers limited guidance for practitioners

Evaluation concerns: reporting 'best validation step' with different validation frequencies per benchmark (potential selection bias); variable training data (50-300 demonstrations) confounds memory contribution with model capacity; limited trial counts for real-world without variance estimates
Cognitive science framing feels post-hoc with loose technical alignment (doesn't implement verbatim vs gist distinction; consolidation differs from biological hippocampal consolidation)
Zero-shot generalization limited (0.47 average on unseen categories, Appendix I) contradicting generalization claims, suggesting potential task distribution overfitting
Comparison fairness issues: π0/π0-FAST use proprioceptive state and wrist cameras; CogACT-Large re-evaluated by authors rather than using original results
No systematic failure analysis: when does temporal modeling hurt? Substantial degradation on camera view shifts (42%) unexplained
